title: Chapter 37
text: ∫ a cat is a cat is a cat is a cat she’s whistling and clapping for the cats at 2 a.m. as I sit in here with my wine and my Beethoven. “they’re just prowling,” I tell her . . . Beethoven rattles his bones in majesty. and those damn cats don’t even care about any of that. and if they did I wouldn’t like them at all: things begin to lose their natural value as they near human endeavor. nothing against Beethoven: he did fine for what he was but I wouldn’t want him on my rug with one leg over his head while he was licking his balls.
